definitions.definition: The 'great seal': the nature of one's own mind — empty, luminous, unborn — and its realization, which 'seals' all phenomena; also the path and instructions leading to it. Phyag is non-dual wisdom seizing (it), rgya is the release of saṃsāra's knot, chen po is union, the self-liberated dharmakāya (Karṇatantravajrapada). Distinct from the haṭha-yoga seal of the same name.
Taught as ground, path and fruit: ground — mind itself, clarity-emptiness; path — the vajra yoga of Mahāmudrā; fruit — the stainless dharmakāya (3rd Karmapa).
The Mahāmudrā 'of the amulet box': ground, path and fruit enclosed together; the mind left uncontrived is self-liberated.

equivalents.note: Kagyu authors (Karma Chagmé, Tselé) treat Mahāmudrā's mind-nature and Dzogchen's rigpa as one in essence; Nyingma and Kagyu authors also distinguish their methods; not an agreed equivalence.

term: tha mal gyi shes pa (ordinary mind)

definitions.definition: 'Ordinary mind': present awareness just as it is, uncontrived and unspoiled by conceptions of worldly or spiritual kinds; recognized, it is the dharmakāya (Gampopa); 'the great way of the ordinary' (Karṇatantravajrapada).

equivalents.note: ordinary mind is the co-emergent mind recognized; 'ordinary' stresses its unfabricated, everyday presence

definitions.definition: The pointing-out or introduction: the guru's direct indication of the nature of mind to the disciple, by which the disciple recognizes it; given in stages in the manuals (mind in stillness and movement, appearances as mind, mind as empty, emptiness as self-liberated).

notes: No standard Sanskrit equivalent; ngo sprod is the Tibetan technical term.

definitions.definition: The Gampopa-lineage instruction that joins the disciple with the co-emergent: mind-as-such is dharmakāya, appearances its light, thoughts its waves; also the name of a Mahāmudrā practice cycle.

cross_language.note: reconstructed Sanskrit; not attested as a title here

definitions.definition: The co-emergent (lhan cig skyes pa): what is born together with — i.e. inseparable from — mind, appearances and thoughts: the dharmakāya present in them; 'co-emergent wisdom' is clarity-emptiness free of grasping (Karṇatantravajrapada).

Mind itself, the nature of mind, as opposed to the moving, dualistic mind (sems): unborn, empty and luminous; 'the basis of phenomena' (Nāropa); 'mind itself unborn and empty is dharmakāya' (Karṇatantravajrapada).

cross_language.note: Sanskrit forms occur in the dohās; usage differs

definitions.definition: sems: the ordinary knowing mind with its thoughts, to be distinguished from its nature (sems nyid); examined in Mahāmudrā vipaśyanā for colour, shape, location, arising, abiding and going.

Awareness: the knowing, clear aspect of mind's nature; in Kagyu Mahāmudrā texts used of self-aware mind (rang rig) that is clear because it is awareness and non-conceptual (Nāropa); 'leave awareness naked' (Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā).

cross_language.note: vidyā is the usual Sanskrit equivalent

notes: U45 owns the Dzogchen sense (rigpa vs sems); this is the Kagyu contribution.

definitions.definition: ye shes, 'primordial knowing': the wisdom that is mind's nature — self-arisen, non-conceptual, clear; distinguished from consciousness (rnam shes), which it becomes when recognized (3rd Karmapa).
rnam shes: dualistic consciousness in its eight kinds, which when recognized are the five wisdoms (3rd Karmapa's Distinguishing Consciousness and Wisdom).
kun gzhi rnam shes: the all-ground consciousness, which recognized is mirror-like wisdom (3rd Karmapa); Nāropa lists the ālaya among the 'situations' of the one mind.

'od gsal, clear light: the luminous nature of all phenomena and of mind, pure from the beginning like space; fivefold (natural, wisdom, samādhi, suchness, realization) and arising at five times (death, the central channel, sleep, one taste, insight); at death, recognizing it as mother and child meeting is dharmakāya buddhahood.

equivalents.note: the sūtra 'luminous mind' and the tantric 'clear light' are identified in the Kagyu (Nāropa: realizing mind itself as clear light); the tantric term adds the death and sleep contexts

definitions.definition: ma bcos pa, 'uncontrived': the mind left as it is, without fabrication, correction or spoiling — the key of Mahāmudrā resting ('relax in the uncontrived natural state', Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā; 'rest undistracted, without fabricating or spoiling', Tilopa's Acintya).
The innate, genuine state of mind, 'uncontrived innate' (ma bcos gnyug ma) in the Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā.

Self-liberation: thoughts and appearances liberate themselves in their own place when their nature is seen; 'the self-liberated dharmakāya' (Karṇatantravajrapada); in the Shangpa, the 'three self-liberations' of the Amulet Mahāmudrā.

rnam rtog, discursive thought: not an enemy to be suppressed; 'the essence of thought is dharmakāya' (Dorje Chang Thungma); like clouds it dissolves in space when one's mind is seen (Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā).

rtse gcig: 'one-pointedness', the first of the four yogas of Mahāmudrā — the mind rests one-pointedly in clarity and emptiness, with experiences of bliss, clarity and non-thought, in lesser, middling and greater degrees.

spros bral: 'freedom from elaboration' or 'simplicity', the second yoga of Mahāmudrā — the mind's nature is realized as rootless, beyond arising, abiding and ceasing, existence and non-existence; Nāropa: 'free of all elaborations'.

equivalents.note: Pali nippapañca is freedom from conceptual proliferation; the Kagyu yoga-name names a stage of realization

definitions.definition: ro gcig: 'one taste', the third yoga of Mahāmudrā — appearances and mind, saṃsāra and nirvāṇa, meditation and post-meditation are realized as of one taste.

'Non-meditation', the fourth yoga of Mahāmudrā — there is nothing to meditate on and no meditator; realization is complete; its greater degree is the dharmakāya; 'by familiarity with non-meditation unsurpassed awakening is attained' (Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā).

yid la mi byed pa, 'non-mentation': not engaging the mind (in grasping); the path of Mahāmudrā 'free of identification, not engaging the mind' (Tilopa); Maitrīpa's cycle of that name is a root of Kagyu Mahāmudrā.
Non-distraction: the 'main body of meditation' (Dorje Chang Thungma); 'without distraction is the king of meditation' (Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā).
dran pa, mindfulness: in dream yoga 'the iron hook of mindfulness' seizes the dream; in Mahāmudrā mindfulness moves from deliberate effort to effortless mindfulness that is not other than awareness.

equivalents.note: Sanskrit and Pali forms of the same term

definitions.definition: Temporary meditative experiences — above all bliss, clarity and non-thought — which come and go and are to be neither sought nor clung to; distinguished from realization (rtogs pa).
Realization: stable, non-fluctuating recognition of the nature of mind, as opposed to passing experiences; each of the four yogas is marked by its realization.
zhi gnas: in Mahāmudrā, calm abiding first with support (object, breath, deity) and then without support, the waves of thought subsiding in their own place.

lhag mthong: in Mahāmudrā, insight that looks directly at the mind in stillness and movement and recognizes its empty, luminous nature — 'looking again and again at the mind that cannot be looked at'.

lta ba, the view: in the view–meditation–conduct–fruition scheme, the recognition of mind's nature; 'beyond grasper and grasped is the king of views' (Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā); a mistaken view misdirects meditation and conduct (Nāropa).
sgom pa, meditation: 'without distraction is the king of meditation'; in Mahāmudrā not the fabrication of a state but becoming familiar (goms pa) with the recognized nature.
spyod pa, conduct: 'without effort is the king of conduct' (Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā); conduct follows the view — from renunciate discipline to the 'madman's conduct' of the realized.
'bras bu, fruition: 'without hope and fear the fruit is manifest' (Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā); the dharmakāya that was always present.
chos sku: the emptiness of mind itself, unborn; 'the essence of thought is dharmakāya'; recognized at death as the clear light by those of highest faculties.
longs sku: the union of emptiness and clarity as baseless great bliss (Karṇatantravajrapada); attained in the bardo by the middling, 'like a fish in water'.
sprul sku: mind's unceasing clear radiance, whatever arises (Karṇatantravajrapada); taking rebirth as emanation; in Tibetan usage also a recognized reincarnate teacher (tulku).
ngo bo nyid sku, the 'essence body': the inseparability of the three kāyas, counted as a fourth; the Shangpa Amulet Mahāmudrā's fruit is the four kāyas.

bde gshegs snying po: buddha-nature, the cause of awakening present in all beings (Jewel Ornament ch.1); identified by Nāropa and the 3rd Karmapa with the luminous emptiness of mind, obscured by adventitious stains.
chos nyid: the clear light of dharmatā without arising and ceasing, beyond speech and thought, is the path of Mahāmudrā (Tilopa).
chos dbyings: the expanse; its stainless wisdom is the fifth wisdom into which the eight consciousnesses resolve (3rd Karmapa).

stong pa nyid: in the Kagyu emptiness is never a blank — it is inseparable from clarity and appearance ('appears yet empty, empty yet appears, like a moon in water', Nāropa); 'emptiness is also mind' (3rd Karmapa).

zung 'jug, union: of emptiness and clarity, appearance and emptiness, bliss and emptiness; in the six yogas the 'body of union' that arises from clear light, first as the learner's then as the non-learner's union.
bde ba chen po, great bliss: the taste of mind's nature 'as it is' (Nāropa); the saṃbhogakāya aspect (Karṇatantravajrapada); the object of the method path.

byang chub kyi sems: (1) the aspiration for awakening for others' sake, aspiring and engaging, relative and ultimate (Jewel Ornament); (2) mind's nature itself, 'the root of all phenomena' (Tilopa); (3) in the completion stage, the white element of the subtle body.
rigs: the potential for awakening, fivefold in the Jewel Ornament (cut off, uncertain, śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, Mahāyāna); even the 'cut off' are not so forever.

gtum mo, 'the fierce one', inner heat: the yoga of kindling heat at the navel, melting the drops and bringing winds into the central channel, 'the main trunk of the path' and 'armour' of the six yogas; restricted practice.

sgyu lus, illusory body: (1) the practice of seeing all appearances and one's body as illusion (mirror image, rainbow, moon in water); (2) the pure illusory body of the deity arising from clear light.

rmi lam, dream: as a yoga, dreams are seized with mindfulness, trained, increased, transformed and emanated, and known as illusion; one who does not know dream as illusion will not know the bardo as illusion.
bar do, the intermediate state: in the Nāropa system three bardos — of birth-and-death (this life), of dream, and of becoming — in which clear light, illusory body and union are to be recognized.

Transference of consciousness at death through the upper aperture to a pure land or to the dharmakāya; 'buddhahood without meditation'; many kinds; to be done only when the time has come — untimely transference 'kills the deities'. Restricted practice.

cross_language.note: Tengyur titles render 'pho ba with saṃkrānti; utkrānti is also used

equivalents.note: Hindu yogic departure of the soul at death through the crown; the Buddhist practice transfers consciousness (not a soul) to a pure land

definitions.definition: 'Entering a town': transference of consciousness into another (dead) body, cast off and taken up like a snake's skin; requires mastery of wind and mind; by the tradition's account it ceased in Tibet with Marpa's son. Restricted.

las kyi phyag rgya, the action seal: practice with a consort, in some lists one of Nāropa's dharmas (the 'method path'); sealed and restricted; the texts warn that the heedless and craving fall to lower realms.
rtsa: the channels of the vajra body; the central channel with the left and right and the four wheels are the key points of inner heat.

rlung, wind: the energy on which mind rides; when winds and mind enter the central channel there is non-conceptuality; the 21,600 daily movements of the five root winds cease into wisdom (Karṇatantravajrapada).
thig le: the drops (white and red essences) of the vajra body; melted by inner heat they give rise to the four joys.
dbu ma / a wa dhU tI, the central channel; entering it, wind and mind give non-conceptuality; the channel-knots released, 'all becomes the central channel'.
The yogas of the channels and winds: the completion-stage body practices on which inner heat rests; restricted.
Magical-wheel (yantra) exercises of the vajra body — in the Karṇatantravajrapada six root and thirty-nine branch movements — for clearing obstacles in the channel-and-wind practices; restricted.

Blending: mixing one practice or state with another — day and night, dream and illusory body, clear light at sleep and at death; 'the five blendings' carried onto the path in the bardo (Karṇatantravajrapada).
Taking onto the path: using whatever arises — dreams, thoughts, afflictions, illness, death — as practice; the Shangpa 'three integrations'; the Drukpa 'six equal tastes'.
Equalizing the taste: the Drukpa practice of meeting adverse circumstances as one taste with the mind's nature (the six cycles of equal taste).
In the Karṇatantravajrapada 'blending and equal taste' are applied to the three pledges; in the bka' dpe phyi ma the 'equal taste of the four elements' is needed for inner heat to progress.

bla ma: the root of blessing and the one who points out the mind; 'devotion is the head of meditation'; qualified by the three trainings and experience; seeing mind directly 'is the guru's kindness' (Tilopa).
The root guru: the teacher from whom one receives the pointing-out and to whom one's devotion is principally directed; without his consent, instructions do not bear fruit (the Ngok episode).
Devotion — longing and respect toward the guru — through which blessing enters; 'the head of meditation'.

cross_language.note: not a translation equivalent; Sanskrit śraddhā/bhakti overlap in part

definitions.definition: byin rlabs, blessing: the transforming influence that flows from the lineage through the guru to the devoted disciple, regarded as the decisive condition for realization of Mahāmudrā.

equivalents.note: Pali adhiṭṭhāna is 'resolve'; the Tibetan sense of transmitted blessing is Mahāyāna/Vajrayāna usage

definitions.definition: dbang, empowerment: the Cakrasaṃvara four empowerments of the sixty-two-deity maṇḍala and those of Vajravārāhī's fifteen goddesses ripen the disciple for the six dharmas (Karṇatantravajrapada).
dam tshig, pledge: kept by practising the guru's instruction 'like the flow of a river'; broken by giving the instructions to unfit vessels.
The whispered or hearing lineage: instructions passed orally from ear to ear, going back to the ḍākinīs and Tilopa; the Rechung, Ngendzong and Dakpo hearing lineages.

cross_language.note: as in the Tengyur titles Tōh 2337, 2338

definitions.definition: 'Lineage of the word': the transmission of the Buddha's word and the gurus' precepts through an unbroken succession of realized teachers; folk etymology dkar brgyud, 'white lineage', after the cotton-clad yogins.
A teacher recognized as the rebirth of a previous master; by the tradition's account the Karmapas were the first such line (Karma Pakshi recognized as Düsum Khyenpa's rebirth).
'The one of (buddha-)activity': the title of the head of the Karma Kagyu, regarded as an emanation of Avalokiteśvara, recognized in successive rebirths since Düsum Khyenpa.
A yogin who wears only a single cotton cloth, sustained by inner heat — Milarepa, Rechungpa and their successors.
Retreat within sealed boundaries — from a session to the three-year retreat — the Kagyu 'practice lineage' form of life.

notes: The formal three-year retreat is recent (Jamgön Kongtrul).

definitions.definition: mkha' 'gro ma, 'sky-goer': the feminine source and guardian of the hearing-lineage instructions — the wisdom ḍākinī to whom Vajradhara speaks the Vajra Verses; Niguma and Sukhasiddhi, source of the Shangpa.
The meditational deity with whom one's mind is bound by pledge — for the Kagyu chiefly Cakrasaṃvara, Vajravārāhī and Hevajra; one of the three roots and of the fivefold Mahāmudrā.

cross_language.note: a later Sanskrit gloss; not a translation equivalent

definitions.definition: rdo rje 'chang: the dharmakāya buddha in sambhoga form, from whom Tilopa received the teaching directly; the speaker of the Vajra Verses; the guru is to be seen as Vajradhara.
chos skyong, Dharma protector: for the Karma Kagyu above all Mahākāla Bernagchen ('the black-cloaked') and for the Shangpa the six-armed wisdom Mahākāla.
nag po chen po: as Bernagchen, the chief protector of the Karma Kagyu; the six-armed form is the Shangpa protector.
'Complete liberation': the sacred biography of a realized master, told as a model for practice (the Lives of Marpa and Milarepa).

cross_language.note: the word; the genre is Tibetan

definitions.definition: Spontaneous songs of realization in the tradition of the Indian dohās — Milarepa's Hundred Thousand Songs, the Kagyu Gurtso.

The preliminaries: the four thoughts that turn the mind and the four special practices (refuge and prostration with bodhicitta, Vajrasattva, maṇḍala offering, guru yoga), usually done a hundred thousand times each, before Mahāmudrā instruction.

term: blo ldog rnam bzhi (four thoughts that turn the mind)

definitions.definition: The precious human life, death and impermanence, karma, and the faults of saṃsāra, contemplated to turn the mind from worldly concerns.
dal 'byor: the freedoms and endowments of a precious human life, eight and ten (Jewel Ornament ch.2).
Revulsion from, or turning away from, attachment to saṃsāra — 'the feet of meditation' (Dorje Chang Thungma).
dge ba'i bshes gnyen: the spiritual friend, the 'condition' of the path, of four kinds according to the disciple's stage (Jewel Ornament ch.3).
skyabs 'gro: taking refuge in the Three Jewels (and in the Kagyu ngöndro also in the three roots), joined with prostrations.
phar phyin: the six perfections as the heart of the 'method' in the Jewel Ornament (ch.12–17).
sa: the ten grounds of the bodhisattva (Jewel Ornament ch.19); correlated, variously, with the four yogas of Mahāmudrā.
The path of method: the tantric yogas of the six dharmas (inner heat and the rest, in some usages specifically the consort practice), paired with the path of liberation (Mahāmudrā).
The path of liberation: Mahāmudrā — recognition of mind's nature through pointing-out and its sustaining through the four yogas.
Interdependent, auspicious connection; the Drukpa 'seven auspicious connections' of Tsangpa Gyare.

cross_language.note: the doctrinal term; the Tibetan colloquial sense 'auspicious coincidence' is wider

equivalents.note: same word, narrower ritual-auspicious sense here

term: dkar po chig thub (the self-sufficient white remedy)

definitions.definition: A medical image for a remedy that alone cures all illnesses: recognition of mind's nature as by itself sufficient for awakening (Gampopa, Lama Zhang).
In Sakya Paṇḍita's critique: a revival of the Chinese Hashang's teaching, not Mahāmudrā.
Strayings in meditation: attachment to bliss, clarity or non-thought, leading respectively to the desire, form and formless realms.
Deviations from emptiness: from its essence, into sealing, into the antidote, and into the path.
Hope and fear — for results and against failure — the last grasping to be released: 'without hope and fear the fruit is manifest' (Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā).
The state in which an accomplished practitioner, after the breath has stopped, remains absorbed in the clear light for days, the body not decaying (the tradition's account).

notes: The term is general Tibetan; its use for post-death absorption is the tradition's.

definitions.definition: In one Karma Kagyu strand (the 8th Situ, Jamgön Kongtrul reading the 3rd Karmapa), the ultimate — buddha-nature — is empty of what is other than it (adventitious stains) but not of its own qualities; contested by others in the school (the 8th Karmapa).

notes: U48 owns the Jonang definition; the id follows the registry's dsp:rangtong-shentong spelling.
